# generator-shortcuts

The strongest plausible rival is **`row_major_first_two`**: select the first two
nonzero cells in row-major spatial order, then apply the same axis, prefix and
periodic-band construction as the intended rule. It fits all five canonical
pairs because every canonical input contains exactly two nonzero cells, so
color-major and row-major selection cannot disagree there.

An exact counterexample is a 17×21 zero grid with only these nonzero cells:

```text
(0,0)=1, (0,19)=8, (2,1)=5, (9,9)=7, (13,10)=9
```

All unlisted cells are zero. The complete JSON input and outputs are in
`repo/generators/c739fcbc6cbd/workspace/counterexamples/row_major_first_two.json`.
The intended color-major rule selects `(0,0,1)` and `(2,1,5)`, producing full
columns alternating 1,5,1,5,… across all 17 rows. The rival selects `(0,0,1)`
and `(0,19,8)`, producing color 1 only in column 0 and color 8 only in column 19
within this width. The outputs therefore disagree.

I checked the intended output three ways: the independent Python `rule_mirror`,
the executable rival comparison, and the canonical Racket authority through
`arcpuzzles apply`. The source-bound Racket receipt is
`checks/counterexample/racket.json`; it records final generator SHA-256
`cbcf3f9249c0f98cdc8bb021e7e16156d5a1e277d7b65abca53ac57ab308bd24`,
executed rule hash `689b63050826`, a valid generator-domain check, and output
SHA-256 `8cfbb64b89e5f09948c56e041f8b8a811f4c2c6cf26227d1390bcb182b99be69`.

Yes, the proposed generator emits such cases. Every explicit
`scene_profile="high_color_decoys"` draw is constructed to make this rival
disagree, and every even default sample index selects that profile. The focused
suite checked 150 explicit decoy draws, and the exhaustive two-slot schedule plus
the 300-lesson census found no surviving declared-rival lesson or query rotation.
This is finite evidence against this rival, not a proof against every possible
shortcut.
